qs.q: What hazard ratios did the study find for incident cardiovascular disease, per standard deviation of the index and for the highest versus lowest quartile, and over how many events and what follow-up?
qs.a: Per SD HR 1.11 (95% CI 1.04-1.17); highest vs lowest quartile HR 1.35 (1.15-1.59); 1384 incident CVD events among 5768 CHARLS participants, median follow-up 9 years

qs.q: How well did the index discriminate incident CVD compared with the cardiometabolic index alone?
qs.a: AUC 0.605 vs 0.603 for CMI (DeLong p=0.104, not significant); optimism-corrected c-index 0.604; incremental IDI 0.0013 (not significant)

qs.q: What happened to the cross-sectional association with advanced CKM stages when Stage 3 was defined only by advanced chronic kidney disease?
qs.a: It was strongly attenuated: per-SD OR 1.086 (95% CI 1.008-1.171) instead of 2.03; the quartile analysis became non-significant (Q4 OR 1.198, p=0.092)

qs.q: Does the paper show that the index predicts CKM stage about twice as strongly as it predicts CVD, given an odds ratio of 2.03 per SD for advanced CKM stages and a hazard ratio of 1.11 per SD for CVD?
qs.a: No. They are different outcomes and different measures (a cross-sectional odds ratio vs a prospective hazard ratio), and the 2.03 is largely inflated by circularity with the Framingham score. The paper makes no such comparison.

qs.q: In the joint analysis of the two components, which groups had a significant CVD risk, and was there an interaction?
qs.a: Only high CMI plus high MLI (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.03-1.46, p=0.0195). High CMI alone (HR 1.16, p=0.073) and high MLI alone (HR 1.05, p=0.57) were not significant. No multiplicative (p=0.510 and 0.934) or additive interaction.

qs.q: Why could NHANES not be used to test prediction of incident CVD?
qs.a: NHANES is a cross-sectional survey with no prospective follow-up for cardiovascular events, so it served only as a cross-sectional replication cohort for advanced CKM stages

qs.q: What limitations do the authors give about the muscle-loss index and its use?
qs.a: It is a surrogate biochemical marker, not a direct measure of muscle mass or diagnosis of sarcopenia (correlation with grip strength only rho=-0.367); creatinine and cystatin C are affected by kidney function, age, inflammation, nutrition; cystatin C is not routinely measured and costs extra

qs.q: Do the authors conclude that a high index value causes cardiovascular disease?
qs.a: No. The design is observational; causal conclusions cannot be drawn, the results are statistical associations, and residual or unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded

qs.q: How was CKM Stage 3 almost entirely classified in CHARLS, and why does that matter?
qs.a: By the Framingham high-risk criterion (2379 of 2386 Stage 3 participants; only 7 by advanced CKD). The Framingham score shares HDL cholesterol with the CMI component, so the cross-sectional association is partly circular

qs.q: What net reclassification improvement did the index achieve over established risk scores?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Net reclassification is not reported (only IDI was); reclassification is listed as future work

qs.q: What was the hazard ratio of the index for all-cause mortality?
qs.a: NOT STATED. All-cause mortality appears only as the competing event in a Fine-Gray sensitivity analysis (HR for CVD 1.097); no mortality hazard ratio is given
